description: Gate pattern generator built on a 15 bit counter: each bit is set to count as high, as low, or not at all, and the output is high whenever the count matches every bit set either way

params.text: Holds the count at zero for as long as it is held down, releasing it to run again
Runs the counter while engaged and holds it while released; engaging it sets the count back to zero
Chooses how that bit of the counter is used: 1 matches while the bit is high, 0 matches while the bit is low, and X leaves the bit out of the pattern

inputs.text: Each rising edge advances the counter by one
A high gate holds the count at zero and it runs again when the gate falls, in parallel with the RESET button
A high gate runs the counter and a low gate holds it; a cable here overrides the RUN button

outputs.text: 10V whenever the count matches every bit switch set to 1 or 0, and 0V otherwise
10V whenever the count fails to match the bit switches, and 0V when it matches them
A 1ms trigger each time the gate turns on

notes: with every bit switch at X there is nothing to match, and the gate output stays at 0V
the divisions this module can produce are long, so it is best driven by a fast clock

inputs.0: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.1: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.2: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
